concepts.title: The European Union
concepts.definition: The European Union evolved from post-war economic cooperation through the 1957 Treaty of Rome into a political-economic union with a common currency, common foreign and security policy and member-driven institutions; the EU is the world's largest economy bloc challenges of integration remain.
concepts.key_idea: The EU integrates by economics first and politics second, pooling sovereignty in trade and currency while nations keep armies.
concepts.textbook_ref: leps102.txt EU evolution, institutions and currency sections
question_patterns: trace the EU's evolution from the Treaty of Rome
name the EU's key institutions and roles
what is the euro and when did it circulate
state the EU's economic and military strengths
discuss limits of EU integration
compare the EU's soft power with US hard power

solution_steps.explain: the 1957 treaty created the EEC that grew into the EU
the euro replaced national currencies across most members
defence and foreign policy remain largely national choices

concepts.title: ASEAN's Way
concepts.section: The Association of South East Asian Nations
concepts.definition: ASEAN, founded in 1967, built regional cooperation through the 'ASEAN way' - consensus, non-interference and informality - creating an ASEAN Free Trade Area and security dialogues like the ASEAN Regional Forum without supranational institutions.
concepts.key_idea: The ASEAN way trades speed for comfort: no member is forced, so all members stay at the table.
concepts.textbook_ref: leps102.txt ASEAN founding, ASEAN way and FTA sections
question_patterns: when was ASEAN founded and by which states
describe the ASEAN way of cooperation
what is the ASEAN Free Trade Area
state the role of the ASEAN Regional Forum
compare ASEAN's and EU's integration models
assess ASEAN's economic and strategic significance

solution_steps.explain: ASEAN formed in 1967 by five Southeast Asian states
the ARF extends ASEAN's convening power to bigger powers

concepts.title: China's Rise
concepts.definition: China's rise rests on the 1978 economic reforms that opened the economy to foreign investment and markets while keeping party control, producing decades of double-digit growth, the world's largest populated military modernisation and global economic weight; integration with the world economy through WTO entry deepened its rise.
concepts.key_idea: Reform without democratisation created a distinctive model: markets in goods, party control in politics.
concepts.textbook_ref: leps102.txt 1978 reforms, growth and WTO entry sections
question_patterns: what changed in China after the 1978 reforms
compute the years between the PRC's founding and the reforms
state the pillars of China's economic rise
how did WTO entry affect China's economy
discuss the China model's political features
evaluate China as an alternative centre of power

solution_steps.explain: Deng's reforms launched in 1978 after the PRC's 1949 founding
special economic zones and exports industrialised the coast
trade surpluses and reserves converted into global influence

concepts.title: Japan and Emerging Centres
concepts.definition: Japan rebuilt as an economic power after 1945 under the US security umbrella, leading in technology and aid despite constitutional limits on military role; South Korea and other Asian economies followed export-led models, adding further centres to a diversifying world economy.
concepts.key_idea: Economic power without matching military power defined Japan's post-war international personality.
concepts.textbook_ref: leps102.txt Japan's rise, constitution limits and Korea sections
question_patterns: describe Japan's post-war economic rise
how does the constitution limit Japan's military

assess the shift from G7 to G20 in world governance

solution_steps.explain: post-1945 Japan industrialised under US protection
the peace constitution constrained overseas military action
Korea and ASEAN economies replicated export-led growth
